newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: FORECAST-SLOVAK 1997 REAL GDP TO GROW 5 PCT - OECD.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-SLOVAK 1997 REAL GDP TO GROW 5 PCT - OECD.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) on Monday forecast Slovakia's real gross domestic product (GDP) to grow at around six percent in 1996, slowing to five percent growth in 1997.

"(Slovakia's) real GDP is projected to grow at around six percent per a year in 1996, supported mainly by stronger domestic demand (including ambitious infrastructure programmes)," the OECD said in its first full economic survey devoted to Slovakia.
The OECD also said the country's GDP was forecast to grow at around five percent in 1997, but did provide an explanation for the expected slowdown in economic growth.
The official Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said last week that Slovakia's real GDP rose 7.1 percent year-on-year in the first half of this year.
But according to SUSR's latest forecast, full-year 1996 real GDP is expected to grow by 6.4 to 7.0 percent, compared to a previous projection of 7.1 percent growth.
The bureau attributed the revision to falling export demand and the central bank's tighter monetary policy.
